To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) unsupervised neural network models of visual processing can be tested with images that are identical to those used in behavioral studies (b) unsupervised non-linear neural networks can generate novel predictions about the interaction between pattern symmetry and spatial frequency (c) unsupervised models of visual processing are consistent with unlearned preferences in bees (d) unsupervised networks generate novel predictions about floral choice behaviour that could be tested in future behavioral experiments.
Unsupervised non linear artificial neural networks capture aspects

(a) the ICA model captures the unlearned preference of bees for radial and concentric pattern shapes, and foliage background, (b) FEBAM captures unlearned preference for concentric pattern shapes and foliage background, and (c) ICA predicts a novel interaction between symmetry and spatial frequency that is consistent with the results of behavioural experiments, and is not captured by FEBAM.
